games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: Who really slashed Jamal's football, and how did the boys discover the truth?
choices: Milo Otieno slashed the ball, and the boys discovered the truth when Ben found a knife with the initials M.O. carved into the handle.
Jamal saw Kofi risk his own safety to free a goat tied to a fence in the smoky yard, and he began to think there was more behind Kofi's abrasive mask than shouting and swagger.
Milo damaged the ball because he felt left out and angry after the others stopped talking to him, and once he confessed he asked whether he could still play with the team.
rounds.answer: Milo Otieno slashed the ball, and the boys discovered the truth when Ben found a knife with the initials M.O. carved into the handle.
rounds.explanation: Ben comes running with a knife carved with the initials M.O., which Jamal recognises as Milo Otieno's. When the boys confront Milo he first denies it, then admits, 'Fine. I did it.'

rounds.prompt: In the interview, why did Amara's grandfather leave the family farm, and how did he first earn money in the city?
choices: Milo damaged the ball because he felt left out and angry after the others stopped talking to him, and once he confessed he asked whether he could still play with the team.
Milo Otieno slashed the ball, and the boys discovered the truth when Ben found a knife with the initials M.O. carved into the handle.
A drought in the 1960s made the crops fail, so the family left the farm, and when they first reached the city her grandfather earned money working as a porter at the market.
rounds.answer: A drought in the 1960s made the crops fail, so the family left the farm, and when they first reached the city her grandfather earned money working as a porter at the market.
rounds.explanation: You combine two details from Amara's interview: the drought that ended the farm and the porter work that fed the family in the city.

rounds.prompt: How did the fire at the neighbour's house change the way Jamal saw Kofi?
choices: A drought in the 1960s made the crops fail, so the family left the farm, and when they first reached the city her grandfather earned money working as a porter at the market.
Jamal saw Kofi risk his own safety to free a goat tied to a fence in the smoky yard, and he began to think there was more behind Kofi's abrasive mask than shouting and swagger.
Milo Otieno slashed the ball, and the boys discovered the truth when Ben found a knife with the initials M.O. carved into the handle.
rounds.answer: Jamal saw Kofi risk his own safety to free a goat tied to a fence in the smoky yard, and he began to think there was more behind Kofi's abrasive mask than shouting and swagger.
rounds.explanation: At the fire Jamal sees Kofi risk his life to free the goat tied to the fence. Afterwards the text says Jamal 'began to see him differently' and wondered if there was more behind Kofi's abrasive mask.
